headlines: PepGen Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Corporate Highlights (investors.pepgen.com, 2026-11-10)
PepGen Announces Pricing of $125 Million Public Offering — 25,000,000 shares (investors.pepgen.com, 2026-11-11)
Why Is PepGen Inc. (PEPG) Stock Down -8.13% Today? — cites the $125M equity offering priced at $5.00 (tickeron.com, 2026-11-13)
gappers.catalyst_detail: On Nov 10 PepGen released positive topline results from the 10 mg/kg multiple-ascending-dose cohort of the Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 trial of PGN-EDODM1 in myotonic dystrophy type 1: mean splicing correction of 46.5% (the highest reported to date in a multiple-dose study), 5 of 6 participants above 20% splicing improvement and 4 above 50% at Week 13, with improvements across vHOT, hand-grip strength, 10MWRT and TUG, and no SAEs, DLTs or treatment discontinuations. An independent DSMB cleared advance into the third and highest 12.5 mg/kg cohort (fully enrolled; results 1H 2027) and approved OLE escalation from 5 to 10 mg/kg. The stock closed Nov 10 at $4.61 from a $2.39 prior close on ~106.5M shares versus a ~1M-share normal day. The same morning the company announced a proposed $125.0M follow-on, priced Nov 11 at $5.00 for 25,000,000 shares. Q3 showed $104.8M cash (runway into 2028), $19.4M net loss, and the FDA's March 2026 partial clinical hold on the US arm of FREEDOM2 still unresolved.
gappers.why: This is offering indigestion, not a thesis change. Management sold 25M new shares at $5.00 into a one-day data spike — roughly a third of the 69.3M-share count — and the deal buyers are now ~20% underwater, so every bounce meets supply from holders whose cost basis is $5.00. The clean data has already been priced and paid for; what is left in the tape is the float that was created to monetize it. The slide is monotonic ($4.61 -> $5.26 -> $5.04 -> $4.36 -> $4.205 -> $3.93), which is the signature of mechanical post-deal distribution rather than a reaction to news — no new PepGen headline has crossed since Nov 11.
gappers.impact: Reads as continued orderly distribution, not a fresh one-day spike and not capitulation. Today's 215,566 shares by ~10:00 ET is extremely light against the ~2.6M prior session and a 7.9M 20-day average (itself inflated by the 106M-share Nov 10 print) — this is drift on no volume, which argues the supply overhang is still working through rather than resolving. Sector read-through is nil: XBI is -0.10% and the move is entirely idiosyncratic, so there is no peer confirmation to trade off. The $5.00 deal price is now overhead resistance, and the next genuine catalysts are distant — FREEDOM-OLE 10 mg/kg safety plus 5 mg/kg clinical data in January 2027 and the 12.5 mg/kg cohort in 1H 2027 — with the FDA partial hold unresolved in between, so there is no near-term event to arrest the fade.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst is seven days stale and is actively being sold rather than bought; the structural readouts are 2-6 months out and the US clinical hold is still open, so nothing here supports a multi-day swing hold in the current Mid-cycle tape (Healthcare is the favored sector, but a post-deal biotech fade is not a Healthcare momentum expression).
gappers.opportunity_cost: The book is 100% cash — $100,000 equity, 0 of 6 positions, 0 open orders — so nothing would be displaced and all 3/3 weekly trade slots are open. The binding cost is the weekly slot itself, and the setup cannot earn it. ATR(14) is $0.621, or 14.25% of price, so the mandated 10% stop (~$3.57) sits at just 0.70 ATR — inside a single day's normal range and near-certain to be stopped out on noise before any thesis resolves. Clearing 2:1 R:R off that stop requires a ~20% move to ~$4.76, which is directly into the $5.00 deal-price supply wall, so the reward leg is capped exactly where the selling lives. It also fails the Entry Checklist on catalyst (the documented catalyst is bullish but already monetized and being distributed) and offers no bullish confluence — buying a sixth down day on no volume is bottom-fishing, which the rulebook forbids. Against today's trend-aligned movers (NIO +4.0%, NBIS +3.5%, CMBT +2.7%) PEPG is the weakest use of a slot. Research only — no order placed (STEP 8).

headlines: Rigetti Computing Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results (globenewswire.com, 2026-11-10)
Rigetti Computing Misses Q3 2026 Estimates as Revenue Falls — $1.4M vs $3.5M expected, -28% YoY (LinkedIn/MarketCatalyst)
Rigetti Computing Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — $497.1M cash, no debt, FY revenue guided to ~$20M (benzinga.com, 2026-11-10)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Rigetti reported Q3 2026 on Nov 10: revenue of $1.41M against roughly $3.5M expected and down ~28% year over year, with gross profit of $857k and adjusted EPS of -$0.06 versus -$0.05 expected. Nine-month revenue is still $10.9M, up 110% from $5.2M, and the balance sheet is genuinely strong at $497.1M of cash and investments with no debt. Management nonetheless reiterated roughly $20M of full-year revenue, which implies a ~$9M Q4 off a $1.4M Q3 — a step-up the market plainly does not believe. The stock has fallen every session since: $12.99 open on Nov 11 to $8.60-8.69 now, about -33%, closing at a 52-day low. Today the entire quantum group is being sold together — IONQ -3.55%, QBTS -3.81%, QUBT -2.67%, RGTI -4.73% — against SPY -0.14% and QQQ -0.14%.
gappers.why: Two mechanisms are stacked. The company-specific one is a credibility break on revenue timing: a 60% miss plus a reiterated full-year guide that needs a 6x sequential jump removes the market's willingness to underwrite the commercialization ramp, and for a pre-revenue story stock the multiple IS the thesis. The sector-wide one is a rotation out of speculative, cash-burning, pre-revenue tech — the quantum complex is down 2.7-4.7% today while the S&P and Nasdaq are flat, which is forced derisking rather than a market move. RGTI is leading the group down because it is the name that just handed the bears a printed number.
gappers.impact: Sustainable direction, but not yet a completed washout. Today's 3.49M shares by ~10:00 ET against a 15.8M 20-day average and a 15.2M prior session is a normal-to-firm pace, not panic volume — there is no capitulation print and no bid stepping in. The sector read-through is the important finding and it is unambiguous: with IONQ, QBTS and QUBT all down 2.7-3.8% on a flat tape, this is a complex-wide repricing, so an RGTI long would be fighting both a single-name credibility problem and a sector outflow at once. Technically there is nothing to lean on — price is below the 20-SMA ($11.44) and far below the 50-SMA ($13.44), at a 52-day closing low, six consecutive down days, with no catalyst between here and the ~March Q4 print to force a re-rate. The $497.1M cash pile removes solvency risk, which is why this bleeds rather than collapses, but cash is not a catalyst.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The driver is sentiment and sector positioning rather than a structural reset — the balance sheet is intact and nine-month revenue is still +110% — but the direction is down, the next verifiable datapoint is a quarter away, and XLK is the worst sector on every horizon (1d, 1mo, 3mo) and has lost its 200-SMA, so nothing supports carrying a long past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Same capacity picture: 100% cash, 0 of 6 positions, 3/3 weekly slots open, nothing to displace. Within today's own list RGTI ranks below PEPG on gap size, and both are down-gaps, so the honest comparison is not PEPG-versus-RGTI but either-versus-nothing — and nothing wins. ATR(14) is $1.137, or 11.82% of price, so the mandated 10% stop (~$7.74) is only 0.76 ATR, inside one day's range on a name that has moved more than 10% intraday twice in the last week. A 2:1 target off that stop needs ~$10.32, which would require retracing nearly the entire post-earnings decline and still lands below the 20-SMA, with a flat-to-down sector pulling the other way — so the reward leg depends on a reversal no evidence supports. It fails the long-bias filter outright (below both the 20- and 50-SMA at a 52-day low), fails the Confluence rule (no bullish indicator agreement and no bullish catalyst — the documented catalyst is a miss), and buying a sixth consecutive down day into an active sector outflow is textbook bottom-fishing. Sector rule 9 also applies in spirit: the quantum/speculative-tech pocket is where today's losses are concentrated, and the rulebook says follow sector momentum, not catch it. Research only — no order placed (STEP 8).
